test_title: PYST 39: SSC MTS 2024 - General Awareness (Held On: 29 Oct, 2024 - Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty mentioned in the Indian constitution?

options.text: To obey parents and discharge our family responsibilities
To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, National Anthem
To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom
To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India

solution:
The correct answer is __**To obey parents and discharge our family responsibilities**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution are enshrined in **Article 51A** under Part IV-A.
 
• They were added through the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• The duties include respecting the Constitution, National Flag, National Anthem, and promoting harmony and brotherhood among citizens, among others.
 
• **Obeying parents and discharging family responsibilities** is a moral duty but not listed as a Fundamental Duty in the Constitution.
 
• Currently, there are **11 Fundamental Duties**, with the 11th duty being added by the **86th Amendment Act, 2002**, which mandates parents/guardians to provide opportunities for education to their children aged 6-14 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• They serve as a reminder to citizens about their responsibilities toward the nation.
 
• Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties are **non-justiciable**, meaning they are not enforceable by law.
 
• The concept of Fundamental Duties in India was inspired by the **Constitution of the erstwhile USSR**.
 
 
 
• **List of Fundamental Duties**
 
 
• Abiding by the Constitution and respecting national symbols.
 
• Promoting harmony and renouncing practices derogatory to women.
 
• Safeguarding public property and striving for excellence in individual and collective activities.
 
 
 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment**
 
 
• Known as the "Mini Constitution," it brought significant changes to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It added the Fundamental Duties and also introduced the concept of the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
 
 
• **86th Constitutional Amendment**
 
 
• Added the 11th Fundamental Duty, which emphasizes education for children aged 6-14 years.
 
• It also made education a Fundamental Right under Article 21A.
